title: 오늘 하루 어떠셨어요?  (How Was Your Day Today?)

segments.t: In the Music Bank control booth, Tak Ye-jin calls the live broadcast — until Cindy flings off the promised jacket on stage and vanishes from the building, leaving Seung-chan to take the heat on his very first day. Listen for the surprised expression for 'already?', and the warm word for 'today's whole day'.
자, 첫 커트는 카메라 포로 갈게요.
수고하셨습니다! 신디 매니저 당장 튀어오라고 해!
벌써? 이것들이 나 무서워서 내뺐네.
방통위는 네가 가면 되겠네.
아까 신디 옷 예쁘다며, 가서 그렇게 얘기해라.
첫 출근이었는데.
오늘 하루 어떠셨어요?
어떠실 것 같으세요?
Let's unpack the eight lines of this chaotic live broadcast finale.
자, 첫 커트는 카메라 포로 갈게요.

'Alright, for the opening shot we'll go with Camera Four.' The opening interjection claps everyone to attention — 'alright, here we go!'. After the word for 'first' opening cut, the closing word ('we will go with') announces the director's choice smoothly to the crew This literally means that.
수고하셨습니다! 신디 매니저 당장 튀어오라고 해!

'Good work, everyone! Tell Cindy's manager to get up here right now!' Right as the song ends, Ye-jin calls out Korea's essential workplace thank-you for hard effort — then explodes in the very next breath, ordering someone to tell him to bounce up here this instant! It is a handy word.
벌써? 이것들이 나 무서워서 내뺐네.

'Already? They were scared of me and bolted.' Hearing Cindy's van already left, she gasps in disbelief — 'already?!'. She follows up with the word for 'scary' and vivid slang for making a getaway It comes from this.
방통위는 네가 가면 되겠네.

'You can be the one who goes to the Broadcast Commission.' Looking around for someone to blame, she lands on poor Seung-chan with a pointed suggestion meaning 'it'll work nicely if you go instead of me!' It comes from this.
아까 신디 옷 예쁘다며, 가서 그렇게 얘기해라.

'Earlier you said Cindy's outfit was pretty, so go tell them that.' The opening word points back to 'earlier today'. attaching a hearsay ending to the word for 'pretty' throws his own words back at him: 'didn't you say it was pretty earlier?' This means that.
첫 출근이었는데.

'It was my very first day at work.' Slumped in his chair afterward, Seung-chan pairs the word for 'first' with 'going to work' and trails off with a wistful past-word ending — letting the sigh finish the sentence This literally means that.
오늘 하루 어떠셨어요?
'How was your day today?' Pairing the word for 'today' with 'one full day' gives you a warm evening check-in, using the respectful past word of the word for 'how is it?' Notice the word for.
어떠실 것 같으세요?

'How do you think it was?' Even exhausted, Seung-chan stays ultra-polite, bouncing the exact same word right back in a respectful 'how do you think it would be?' phrasing — the politest deadpan comeback in Korean television! This means that. Now let's listen to the whole control-booth meltdown again.
자, 첫 커트는 카메라 포로 갈게요.
수고하셨습니다! 신디 매니저 당장 튀어오라고 해!
벌써? 이것들이 나 무서워서 내뺐네.
방통위는 네가 가면 되겠네.
아까 신디 옷 예쁘다며, 가서 그렇게 얘기해라.
첫 출근이었는데.
오늘 하루 어떠셨어요?
어떠실 것 같으세요?

You learned the workplace thank-you after a job well done, the surprised gasp for 'already?', the word for earlier today, and the warm evening check-in asking how the day went. Let's check in on Cindy and Joon-mo next!
안녕히 계세요!
